introduction1.message: Ah, a fresh face! You look like the adventuring type. I'm Marvin, head of the Exploration Guild.
introduction1.opt1: Tell me more about this guild.
introduction1.opt2: I'll figure it out myself. Just show me the tasks.

introduction2.message: The Exploration Guild assigns hunting contracts to capable adventurers. Slay the target, earn Explorer Tokens. Simple as that. Every 5 completed contracts raise your Guild rank — I'll send you into new territory and open more of the guild store.

default.message: Back for more work, or just browsing? The guild always has contracts available.
default.coldForge: Can you check Phurgo's last Slatefall delivery?
default.sealReminder: What did the Pathfinder's Seal teach me?
default.quietRoadSatchel: That Guild runner's satchel. I've got it.
default.sameWinterEnd: Corwin sent this down with me.
default.quietRoadOffer: Anything the Guild needs doing up the Pass?
default.aboutPosting: Why are you really in La Harpar?

whatIsThisPlace1.message: We map the unknown and thin out the dangers. Every monster you hunt under our contract earns you Explorer Tokens. Complete enough tasks and I'll authorize expeditions into deeper, more dangerous territories.

taskIntro.message: Pick a contract length and I'll assign you a target from the regions your rank allows. Tougher regions pay more tokens per contract.
taskIntro.short: Short contract — 25 to 50 kills, 1 Token per region tier.
taskIntro.medium: Medium contract — 50 to 200 kills, 2 Tokens per region tier.
taskIntro.long: Long contract — 200 to 400 kills, 3 Tokens per region tier.

taskInProgress.message: Still hunting. Keep at it — finish the contract and come back to collect your tokens.

taskClaimed.message: Fine work out there! Hand over your finished contracts and I'll pay out the tokens.

coldForgeRecord.message: Phurgo's last Slatefall load: worked iron and his own tools, recorded here before the road closed. He can work salvage while the mine stays shut, but get him to stop for a meal first. One Fish & Apple Pie should do it; the recipe is sold here in La Harpar.

sealRegistered.message: Your name's in the salvage register. Look along the grain, check the seams, and keep the pieces somebody else would pass over. There's sound work out there, if you know where to look.

sealReminder.message: Look along the grain and check the seams; sound work is often overlooked. Once you've learned to spot it, the lesson stays with you. Another seal won't teach it twice.

coldForgeSalvage.message: We map the unknown and bring useful things home. A Pathfinder's Seal earns a place in our salvage register and a lesson in spotting sound gear. Lirold's Arena keeps a few among its prizes, and whoever earns one on the sand brings it to me.

quietRoadOffer.message: Say you're keeping the books for a road. Every cart, every load, every stamp at every post. One winter a whole post stops stamping. No cart through it, nothing back out. Not one line in two years. What do you do?

quietRoadOffer2.message: Right, and somebody has to. The Guild kept a post halfway up the Mountain Pass. A runner called Hobb carried the Mawood post down through it, every month for six years. He was never once late. He set out two winters back and that's where my book stops. The post's still up there, what's left of it. Every post keeps a daybook, under the floor stone, where a runner knows to look and a goblin doesn't. Find it and bring it to me.
quietRoadOffer2.opt2: Two years is a long time to leave a man on a mountain.

quietRoadWhy.message:
It is. I wasn't here for it. I was out past where anybody has a map, and I came home to a letter telling me to stay put and find out what happened on that road. So I'm finding out. I'd go up myself if…

Well. You're going.

quietRoadProgress.message: The post sits off the road on the Pass, a hut, stone below and timber above. If the timber's gone, the stone's still there. Look under the floor.

quietRoadDaybook.message:
That's his hand. "Up from Mawood, bound for the coast. Goblins on the switchbacks. Going round by the cleft." And that's the last line anyone wrote in it.

Say you're a runner with a satchel, and there's goblins on the road. You don't fight them. You go the way carts can't. There's a cleft behind the switchbacks; I've never seen it, only read about it in here, runners' business. If the goblins found it too, that's where your satchel is. Higher up the Pass than you'll want to be.

quietRoadHobbMaybe.message: Then you tell me, and I'll write it down properly, and I'll be the one to tell the Bartender why she isn't getting paid. Bring the satchel either way.

quietRoadProgress2.message: The cleft. Behind the switchbacks, past the halfway mark. Narrow enough that a goat turns sideways. Look for where the rock's worn smooth.

quietRoadSatchel.message:
That's Guild leather, and that's the Pass stamp. Two winters old. He made the post, then. Somewhere below it…

There's a letter in here, still sealed. "To the Exploration Guild." From Mawood, past the Pass, by the look of the wax. Not ours to open. Ours to carry. I'll close Hobb's line in the book tonight. You take this where it was going.

quietRoadWho.message: The wax has a leaf pressed in it, and I've only seen that on one man's post: the elder up there, Corwin. If he sealed it, he expected an answer, and for two years he hasn't had one. Go and give him one.

sameWinterEnd.message:
Another one. Same leaf in the wax. And look at that hand, he's pressed so hard he's nearly gone through the paper. "To the Exploration Guild, Lirold."

Not me, then. Her.
sameWinterEnd.opt2: You're the Guild, as far as I've seen.

sameWinterVarrow.message: Odile Varrow. She runs the Guild from the capital, down the coast road from the beach. She sent me home to watch the Pass road, and I've watched it, and you're what I've got to show her. Take it to her yourself. She'll ask how far it is from the nest to her east gate. Think before you answer.

aboutPosting.message: Because the Guildmaster told me to be. I came home off that last trip wanting a bed and a month of nobody asking me anything, and there was her letter on the table. Stay in La Harpar. Watch the Pass road. Write down every cart that doesn't come down it and every rumour from the north. Say you're her. Three runners gone in two winters, and your traders telling you the trees up there are bleeding. You'd want someone sitting at the bottom of that road with a book. So I sat.

aboutPostingNow.message: Now I've a letter in my book with your name next to it, and Hobb's line is closed. That's more than I had at midsummer.
